name: How do I know which shower base will fit where my old tub was?

mainEntity.name: How do I know which shower base will fit where my old tub was?

acceptedAnswer.text:
The shower base must work with the drain position, room dimensions, entry direction, finished wall thickness, and chosen enclosure. A base that appears to fit on paper may fail because of framing, door clearance, plumbing access, or the finished tile assembly.

Key factors:
- Measure from framing and account for finished wall thickness.
- Confirm drain center, threshold, curb, and entry dimensions.
- Check whether the base is compatible with the planned waterproofing system.
- Coordinate the base with the glass or door manufacturer’s requirements.

Have Elite Remodeling & Design verify the base and enclosure together before ordering. Early product coordination helps prevent costly substitutions after demolition.
acceptedAnswer.description: The base must match the drain, framing, finished wall thickness, entry clearance, waterproofing approach, and enclosure. Verify those dimensions from the existing structure before ordering; a paper measurement alone may not reveal access or framing conflicts.
